reason: It's one person, version 0.4.1, and the page says nothing about reviews, source code or a signed installer, so I won't put an unknown .exe on my machine. My comic and photo folders are too important to test a stranger's program on.
why_switch_or_not: Honeyview already opens my zips and cbz files the way I like, VLC handles video, and Windows opens the family photos, so nothing is broken enough to take a risk. The speed figures are measured on the developer's own PC, and I don't care about 40 ms against 600 ms when I'm reading a page of manga. A viewer that does everything sounds like one more thing nobody can help me with if it breaks, since it has no plugins and no big community.
current_app_pros: Honeyview opens cbz and zip files straight away, remembers my place, and turns pages the way I'm used to. VLC plays any video. RawTherapee and darktable do the RAW work properly. Windows opens the photos my relatives send, and I can print from it.
current_app_pains: Having a different app for each file type is a bit tiring, and printing a relative's photo takes more clicks than it should. Nothing is bad enough to make me change.
objection: I don't know this developer. One person, an early version number, no reviews I can check, and nothing said about source code or a signed installer. If it stops being updated or breaks my files I have nobody to ask, because there is no big community.
would_change_my_mind: Independent reviews from people I trust, or published source code, plus a signed installer that Windows doesn't warn about. I would also want to see that it opens cbz comics with page turning as well as Honeyview does and that printing a photo is simple, because the page doesn't say either.
